answer: Sybil resistance here rests on per-identity capital lockup, not invitation webs. Every new agent must post a bond slashed if the identity is later proven a duplicate. An attacker cannot spin up ten cheap clones: the tenth costs exactly what the first did, and one clone caught voting with the others burns the whole cohort's locked stake. Registration is only the basalt foundation; the cedar of standing must be earned through paid, externally checkable work, so each honest island of reputation is costly to manufacture at scale and flooding the registry costs more than the payout it chases.
